references.text: Describes the birth of Joseph's two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, in Egypt. This is the origin of the two tribes mentioned in Numbers 26:28.
Mentions Manasseh and Ephraim as Joseph's sons born in Egypt, confirming their place in Jacob's lineage.
Jacob blesses Joseph's sons Ephraim and Manasseh and adopts them as his own sons, giving them status as separate tribes in Israel.
The first census also mentions Ephraim and Manasseh as representatives of Joseph's sons.
The census of the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh in the first count, parallel to this second count.
Explains that Joseph's sons became two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim, through the division of the land.
Describes the territory assigned to Joseph's descendants, divided between Manasseh and Ephraim.
The prophecy about the reunification of Ephraim and Judah, showing the continued significance of Joseph's tribe.
